paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this whole sermon. Jesus tells His four disciples the hard stuff BEFORE it happens, so nothing catches them off guard. Wars, earthquakes, famines, even family turning on family: He calls the early ones "the beginning of birth pains," and that means they are not the finish line (Mark 13:7-8). Then He ends with "I have told you everything in advance" (Mark 13:23). That's a teacher who cares more about you being ready than about you being comfortable.

So what do we do with that? The first thing Jesus says is "See to it that no one deceives you" (Mark 13:5). He circles right back to it, warning that false Christs and false prophets will perform signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, "if that were possible" (Mark 13:22). Loud and impressive is not the same as true, friend. The cure is knowing what Jesus actually said, and that's why I keep my nose in the Word.

And listen to the promises tucked in there, because they are the good part. When they're arrested, the Holy Spirit gives them the words to speak (Mark 13:11). The days are cut short by the Lord for the sake of His elect (Mark 13:20). And "the one who perseveres to the end will be saved" (Mark 13:13). I can't tell you when anything happens, because that's not mine to know. I can tell you that my ovens stay ready, and yours can too. The teaching isn't over, so keep that apron on.
